text:
Sam: Quick sync — proposal: introduce a time-bounded resident write lease (TTL) + explicit consent header so proxies can decide fallback behavior when a tenant's resident region is unreachable. Thoughts?
Maria: high-level: sounds good. main risk is accidental cross-border writes if TTLs too long or clocks drift.
Kevin: agree re clocks. We should make lease issuance authoritative from residency service and include monotonic lease-id in header.
Anya: ok but operationally, what are the fallback options? queue locally? redirect to non-resident region with consent? degrade to read-only?
Sam: list I had in mind: 1) Hold and retry at proxy for lease TTL (best for short blips). 2) Escrow write to a consented non-resident region with `X-Residence-Mode: soft-allow` and audit tag. 3) Fail fast with 409 + user-friendly message to app when policy forbids.
Jun: we also need a path for analytics/telemetry: shadow write to analytics store even if resident denies production write — but that can leak PII if consent not present.
Maria: exact header suggestion: `X-Residence-Lease: <lease-id>;ttl=<secs>` and `X-Residence-Decision: enforce|soft-allow|deny`. Caller supplies `X-Consent-Token` when user consent is explicit.
Kevin: proxy pseudo-code: 
```
if (residentUp(tenant)) forwardToResident();
else if (decision == "soft-allow" && consentTokenValid()) forwardToNonResidentShadow();
else if (ttlLeft > 0) queueLocally();
else return 409;
```
Sam: +1 to queueLocally up to small TTL. Need backpressure signals to clients so retries don't thundering-herd.
Anya: stateful queues at proxies blow up at scale. Prefer pushing to a regional durable queue service with small retention (SQS/Kafka). Proxy only returns 202 + lease metadata.
Jun: what about long outages? policy should include an operator-visible escalation: after X hours, tenant enters manual review and we stop soft-allow to avoid permanent cross-border writes.
Maria: agree. Add `X-Residence-Trace` header for audit entries and link to tenant's compliance ticket.
Kevin: how about reconciliation? if we allowed soft-allow writes to non-resident, we need eventual reconciliation/skipping duplicate detection. Use write UUIDs and idempotency keys with origin-region tag.
Sam: that implies the resident region needs a repair ingestion path that can accept out-of-order writes with conflict resolution rules (last-wins only if consented; otherwise operator flag to merge).
Anya: ops concerns: we must expose per-tenant metrics: percent of writes that used soft-allow, queue-depth, avg queue wait, cross-border write volume. These feed billing & compliance dashboards.
Jun: can we enforce TTLs server-side too? e.g., residency service refuses to renew a lease if we've already flagged tenant as in-review.
Maria: yes: residency service should be the single source of truth. Renewals require active heartbeat from edge proxy and operator override window.
Sam: deployment plan idea: 1) Add headers + feature-flag proxies. 2) Pilot with internal tenants and one low-risk customer. 3) Add queued-retry infra and reconciliation job. 4) Add operator escalation + dashboard.
Kevin: testing: need chaos test where resident region becomes partitioned for N minutes and we verify no accidental permanent cross-border writes. Also test clock skew scenarios.
Anya: runbook: include steps to list affected tenants, revert soft-allow via feature flag, and replay queued writes into resident once healthy (or purge if flagged non-consent).
Sam: open questions: default policy for new tenants? keep default as `enforce` (fail fast) and allow `soft-allow` opt-in. We should require explicit consent token to opt-in.
Jun: legal check: need to store consent tokens and link them in audit trail for any soft-allow write.
Maria: I'll draft a minimal schema for headers + decision matrix and push an RFC follow-up.
Sam: thanks. Next actions: Maria to draft RFC, Kevin to sketch reconciliation design, Anya to propose queue infra, Jun to contact legal about consent retention. I'll schedule a short follow-up next week. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary deploy of residency-proxy v0.1 flag-safe scheduled for 1711020000 (noops)
Maria: noted. I'll include an example `curl` snippet in the RFC showing `X-Residence-Decision: soft-allow` + `X-Consent-Token`.
Kevin: one last note — add `X-Idempotency-Key` as required for soft-allow path. saves us a lot of headache.
Sam: agreed. That is it for now.
